findings.title: TRM Labs: North Korea Steals USD 6.36 Billion From Binance in Largest Hack in History
findings.summary_md: On October 29, 2026, an attacker moved about $6.36 billion out of Binance wallets across ten blockchains, the largest crypto theft on record. TRM Labs attributes the attack with high confidence to North Korea's TraderTraitor group, noting most funds moved in about 20 minutes. The amount exceeds the $1.5 billion Bybit heist from February 2025 by roughly four times.

findings.title: Chainalysis: Binance Hack Tracing the $6.4 Billion Theft to North Korea
findings.summary_md: Chainalysis reports the attack began around 4:20 p.m. ET on October 29, 2026, with approximately $6.4 billion moved out of Binance hot wallets across multiple blockchains. The firm links the theft to North Korea's TraderTraitor, matching signatures from earlier state-linked heists and tracing rapid cross-chain outflows.

findings.title: Bloomberg: Binance Suspends Deposits, Withdrawals After $6.3 Billion Hack
findings.summary_md: Bloomberg reported on October 29 that hackers siphoned $6.3 billion from Binance in the largest crypto industry heist ever recorded. Binance founder Changpeng Zhao acknowledged the incident looked like a hack and said the exchange temporarily suspended all deposits and withdrawals.

findings.title: The New York Times: Binance Suspends Withdrawals After Crypto Hackers Steal $6.3 Billion
findings.summary_md: The New York Times reported October 29 that Binance halted withdrawals after hackers stole more than $6 billion in cryptocurrency. The company described it as a security incident, with blockchain partners helping freeze roughly $3 billion of the affected assets.
